intent: Add root-confined repository observation and deterministic evidence drift analysis
Observe root-confined repository files and analyze deterministic evidence drift

name: RepositoryObserver
role: Builds a canonical-root snapshot of regular repository files and their tracking state.
conditions: It skips .git, excludes symbolic links, and returns diagnostics instead of crossing or failing the requested boundary.

name: GitCliTrackingReader
role: Reads tracked paths through the local Git executable.
conditions: Git failures are returned as diagnostics so callers can identify incomplete tracking data.

name: EvidenceDriftAnalyzer
role: Compares resolved concept source-path evidence with repository files.
conditions: It sorts findings and withholds untracked claims when Git tracking is incomplete.

subject: Tracking completeness
why: A missing Git result cannot prove that an observed file is untracked, so the report marks incompleteness rather than asserting drift.

title: Confine repository observation to canonical regular files
why: Canonical-root traversal, .git exclusion, and no-follow-link regular-file checks keep every observed path inside the supplied repository boundary.
alternative: Follow symbolic links or traverse raw paths — rejected because they can expose files outside the requested repository.

title: Expose incomplete Git tracking instead of false untracked drift
why: The analyzer emits untracked evidence only after Git produced complete tracking data; otherwise it returns diagnostics and marks the report incomplete.
alternative: Treat all non-reported files as untracked — rejected because unavailable Git data cannot prove a file is untracked.

title: Promote root-confined repository inspection
why: The canonical-root and no-follow-link boundary is a reusable inspection rule for every repository-root request.
alternative: Treat root confinement as a one-off observer detail — rejected because every repository inspection must preserve the requested boundary.
